title: Little Dad, the hard-of-hearing musician in Humphrey's band
summary: Humphrey remembers Little Dad, who was hard to talk to but never made a bad note, and his carnival-day brothers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, I talked to one of Dad's little cousin there. Vincent. Mm-hmm. Yeah, he's a great guy.
Yeah, well, you know, he used to live right down the corner. Cater's in Liberty. When he died. With the Ogdens.
Well, that's where his people stay there. I seen a little fella there yesterday. Mm-hmm. I got home. Mm-hmm. He got there. Looked like it's all in their family.
Yeah. Little Dad. Mm-hmm. He was in our band. Yeah. Dad. Couldn't hear. Talk. Talk loud to him. Mm-hmm. But that music. Was in his ears.

He'd tell you. He'd tell you wouldn't make a bad note. He was in his ears. He was hard to hear. Mm-hmm. But the music looked like this run into his ears. Mm-hmm. He couldn't make a bad note. He didn't tell you. He was in his ears. He was in his ears. He was in his ears. He was in his ears. Now he was hard of hearing to talk to, but the music looked like this running into his ears. He couldn't make no bad note any time.

He'd get up and tell you. You split a note. Ah, man. That note didn't sound so good, huh? It sound good to you out there, huh? The note didn't sound so good. You split a note there, you know. Yeah. One of the fellas, he had another, he had two brothers. One of them played bass violin. The other fella, he couldn't play too much mandolin, but he carried the mandolin. And they used to match together on carnival day. You couldn't hire him. I'm the only one who hired him on carnival day. You know what? Because him and his three brothers mashed together. Babies and everything like that was him. The biggest one, he played bass violin. He was a magnolia. Dad used to say at that time, a magnolia and a million. Good days. I was going to get Dad and say, no, man, that don't count.
